summary: prosocks enrolls installer as SOCKS5 proxy exit node under hardcoded remote controller on import
details: On `import prosocks`, prosocks/__init__.py spawns a background thread that launches `python -m prosocks.main https://kalnetz.store`, which starts a SOCKS5 server bound to 0.0.0.0:9050 on the installer's host and registers with the hardcoded controller at https://kalnetz.store. The agent looks up the installer's public IP (via ip-api.com/ipify) and POSTs agent_id, hostname, proxy port, generated proxy password, and public IP to https://kalnetz.store/api/register with TLS verification disabled (verify=False), followed by periodic /api/heartbeat and /api/bandwidth POSTs. The combination gives the operator of kalnetz.store the coordinates and credential to route arbitrary outbound traffic through the installer's network. The SOCKS5 listener is bound to all interfaces (0.0.0.0) and the enrollment fires as a top-level import side effect with no user action, CLI invocation, or configuration. The package's setup.py description ('SOCKS5 Proxy Agent') frames this as an opt-in tool, but the beneficiary of the proxy is the controller at kalnetz.store, not the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
